EARLIER: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. inspected San Francisco High School in Quezon City after it took damage from a fire that occurred last June 15.

The fire broke out in the school a day before the opening of classes for School Year 2025-2026.

📷: Presidential Communications Office

President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. visits the fire-hit San Francisco High School in Quezon City on Wednesday, June 17, to assess the situation and monitor ongoing recovery efforts.

During the inspection, Marcos directs Education Secretary Sonny Angara to implement immediate restoration measures for the affected classrooms.

Courtesy: Presidential Communications Office

More photos during the visit of President @bongbongmarcos at the fire-damaged building of San Francisco High School in Quezon City on Wednesday (June 18, 2025). He ordered the @DPWHph to lead the construction of a new four-story building, estimated to cost around PHP180 million and serve some 1,500 students. 

Department of Education Secretary @sonnyangara, @QCMayorJoy Joy Belmonte and principal Dr. Marissa Lou Rodriguez accompanied the President. | PNA photos by @Robertalfiler1

data.text:
From Tragedy to Triumph: A New Beginning for Students

PBBMs swift response brings renewed hope to 1,500 students, as a new four-story school building rises to replace the fire-damaged structure in Quezon City.

After a devastating fire at San Francisco High School in Quezon City, PBBM acted swiftly, directing the DPWH to construct a new four-story building worth ₱180 million. 
This future-ready facility will serve 1,500 students, restoring hope and ensuring uninterrupted learning. Joined by Secretary Sonny Angara @DepEd_PH and Mayor Joy Belmonte, the President’s visit affirmed the government’s commitment to education. 

In the face of loss, a stronger, safer school will soon rise proof that recovery begins with decisive action.

#BagongPilipinas 🇵🇭
